strategy.summary: The bug is in mathjs isInteger: it uses strict numeric equality, so floating-point roundoff such as (0.1 + 0.2) * 10 = 3.0000000000000004 is incorrectly reported as not an integer. PR #3575 fixes isInteger by comparing with the tolerance-aware equal function. Reproduction adds the PR's new isInteger test assertions while leaving the two src files unchanged, then runs the source unit test command. On buggy commit 095ccb6 the new assertions fail; on the fixed commit they pass.

The bignumber variants fail similarly because the Number passed to bignumber already carries the roundoff error.
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: After applying the source changes from PR #3575, the added assertions pass: isInteger((0.1 + 0.2) * 10) is true, isInteger((0.1 + 0.2) * 10 - 3) is true, and the bignumber variants are true. The existing assertion isInteger(0.1 + 0.2) is still false because 0.1 + 0.2 itself is genuinely not close to an integer in a way that changes the expected result.

strategy.summary: isNaN() incorrectly handles non-number types (Units, Complex, BigNumber) inside Array/Matrix because the Array|Matrix overload deep-maps Number.isNaN directly over the elements. Number.isNaN returns false for every non-number object, so a NaN-valued Unit inside a Matrix is reported as not-NaN. At the buggy commit, the new PR test 'should test isNaN element wise on a Matrix of units' fails: isNaN(math.matrix([new Unit(3, 'ft'), new Unit(NaN, 'ft')])) returns math.matrix([false, false]) instead of math.matrix([false, true]).
